svg.title: Prokinetic and antidiarrheal drugs: speed a slow gut with a D2 antagonist (metoclopramide or domperidone), a 5-HT4 agonist (prucalopride) or erythromycin, never with bleeding, obstruction or perforation; slow or dry diarrhea with opioid agonists (loperamide, diphenoxylate, eluxadoline), bismuth subsalicylate or bile acid resins; each with when to choose it and what rules it out

svg.text: a prokinetic must COORDINATE motility: simply boosting acetylcholine only gives uncoordinated contraction
